description: Returns every maintenance window with its schedule, whether it is active, monitorIDs (the monitors it suppresses) and statusPageSlugs (the status pages that announce it). A window with an empty monitorIDs list suppresses nothing. Use it to find the ID that updateMaintenanceWindow, setMaintenanceWindowActive and deleteMaintenanceWindow take; fields returns only the fields you name. Filter by keywords in the title, or by status, e.g. "scheduled,under-maintenance" to leave out ended windows. Returns up to 50 windows per call; pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next page.

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous call, for the next page

fields.description: Only these fields, comma-separated, e.g. "title,active,monitorIDs"; id is always returned. Default: every field.

keywords.description: Space-separated keywords matched against the window's title, case-insensitively; all must match

status.description: Only windows in these statuses, comma-separated: inactive, scheduled, under-maintenance, ended, unknown

name: listMaintenanceWindows

count.description: How many windows this page holds

maintenanceWindows.description: Array of maintenance windows; with fields, only the fields asked for

active.description: Whether the maintenance window is active

dateRange.description: Date range [startDate, endDate] in ISO format, null for recurring windows

intervalDay.description: Interval in days for recurring-interval strategy

monitorIDs.description: IDs of the monitors this window suppresses

status.description: Where the window is now: inactive, scheduled, under-maintenance, ended or unknown

statusPageSlugs.description: Slugs of the status pages that announce this window while it is in effect

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page; absent on the last page

total.description: How many match the filters, across every page

title: List Maintenance Windows
